title: Auto-submit for lone moves
description: When the engine asks a seat a question with exactly one possible answer (a strategic action it must take, or a single system to activate), the web client now answers it for the player and shows a corner toast. The engine still asks; the answer is an ordinary recorded choice. All shots are the real app against a mocked game.

shots.heading: Lone strategic action
shots.caption: The turn menu held only the bare strategic option (no pass, tactical, component or trade). The client sent it and the toast reads "Only one choice: take your strategic action".

shots.heading: Lone system activation
shots.caption: The tactical action was open and exactly one system could be activated. The client activated it; the toast reads "Only one choice: activate system 37".

shots.heading: Setting, on (default)
shots.caption: The player sheet header has a new toggle next to Sound and Toasts: "Auto" (lone moves are taken for you). It is remembered in this browser only.

shots.heading: Setting, off
shots.caption: With the toggle off ("Auto off") the same lone decision stays on the turn bar and nothing is sent.

shots.heading: A normal menu still asks
shots.caption: Strategic plus tactical and pass is a real choice: nothing is sent and there is no toast.

shots.heading: After an undo
shots.caption: An undo that lands on the lone decision (there is something to redo) is asked, never answered again, so the player can keep undoing.

notes.title: When it acts
notes.text: Only for the seat's own client, only when the game moved forward to the decision (the history cursor grew with nothing to redo). A page load, a reconnect without progress, an undo, a redo and a restore never trigger it. Each decision is evaluated once, after a 0.4 s pause, and a second tab of the same seat is held back by a claim in localStorage; the server's nonce and version checks still apply.

notes.title: Not changed
notes.text: No engine or server change: histories, replay, bots and undo are unaffected. The server's own auto-resolve notes are separate.
